title: Adaptive Slot Allocator for Sequence Slimming and Prefill-aware Kernel Handoffs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: In high-throughput serving the dominant cost is wasted compute and memory due to padding when requests of widely varying sequence lengths are grouped. Existing approaches reduce padding by coarse bucketing, but they either increase tail latency or require expensive global coordination. This ticket implements an on-host Adaptive Slot Allocator (ASA) that performs lightweight local sequence slimming and prefill-aware kernel handoffs to cut padding without regressing latency SLOs.

Goals: (1) Reduce mean padded-token overhead across workloads with bimodal/long-tailed sequence distributions by at least 25% relative to current length-based bucketing; (2) Preserve p99 latency within current SLOs for both prefill and decode phases; (3) Integrate kernel hinting so runtime can pick smaller-kernel variants when slimmed slots are used; (4) Be deployable as a per-instance runtime optimization with feature flag for canary rollout.
technical_notes: ASA maintains a short local histogram (32 buckets) of recent sequence footprints and computes an adaptive slot table mapping incoming requests to micro-slots in a single pass.

Sequence slimming: at admission time ASA decides a conservative token trim budget (typically 0-8 tokens) per request based on request entropy, priority, and downstream quality budget; trims are only applied when prefill stage allows (no function calls / structured output expected) and user quality budget flag is enabled.

Prefill-aware scheduling: ASA tags requests that will later enter decode with 'prefill-complete' marker; runtime schedules kernel handoff so prefill uses dense kernels and decode can use smaller, memory-packed kernels when KV cache fits compacted layout.

Kernel hinting: ASA emits lightweight affinity hints (e.g., small-kernel-eligible, medium, full) so the kernel-selection layer can pick different CUDA/ROCm kernels optimized for shorter sequence windows, reducing per-token kernel-launch overhead.

Fallback safety: any slimmed request carries metadata to rehydrate tokens at decode if model emits OOV or quality regressions; this supports rollback without user-visible errors but adds cost only on mispredictions.
Stateful metrics: ASA records per-request trimmed_tokens, rehydration_count, kernel_hint chosen, and padding_saved to be emitted to Console for rollout monitoring.
Implementation: prototype as C++ subcomponent behind the existing admission controller; small state (few KB) per worker; feature-flag controlled and switchable via Console rollout.
Interactions: must respect Dedicated capacity isolation (no cross-tenant rebalancing) and Private deployment KMS/audit constraints (no user data sampled in histograms).
acceptance_criteria: Integrated ASA into serving runtime behind a feature flag and default-off in production.
Benchmarks showing >=25% reduction in padded tokens for synthetic bimodal workload and >=15% on real mixed-traffic pilot cluster.
No more than 5% increase in p99 end-to-end latency during prefill or decode phases in canary runs (measured per-route and per-model).
Kernel-selection correctly receives hints and switches to small-kernel variants in at least 90% of eligible cases in test harness.
Console displays new ASA metrics (trimmed_tokens, pad_saved, rehydration_rate) and alerts on rehydration_rate > 2%.
Design doc and security review completed; rollout plan with canary and kill-switch documented.
Unit + integration tests covering trim/no-trim paths, rehydration, and kernel-hint plumbing included in PR.
risks_and_mitigations: Quality regressions from trimming: mitigate by conservative default trim budgets, QA evals on representative prompt sets, and automatic rollback if regression metrics cross threshold.
Increased decode complexity (rehydration cost): mitigate by only allowing rehydration on mismatch cases and monitoring rehydration_rate from canaries.
Kernel compatibility: mitigate by shipping kernel-hinting as best-effort — scheduler must gracefully ignore hints if kernel variant unavailable.
Tenant isolation concerns for Dedicated/Private: ASA must not export raw prompts in telemetry; histograms are aggregated and bounded by count and time windows.
tests_and_metrics: Synthetic benchmark: bimodal seqlen mix (20% short 16 tokens, 80% long 1024 tokens) measure padded_tokens_per_request baseline vs ASA.
Real traffic pilot: 3-node canary cluster over 72 hours with production routing; track pad_saved, trimmed_tokens, rehydration_rate, latency p50/p95/p99, and token-throughput.
SLO targets: pad_saved >= 25% (synthetic) and >=15% (pilot), p99 latency delta <= +5%, rehydration_rate <= 2%.
A/B quality evals: run 50k labeled prompts across trimmed and untrimmed paths; measure top-line accuracy/quality deltas and surface worst-case prompt types.
CI tests: add deterministic unit tests for slot-table generation, greedy trim logic, and kernel-hint emission.
Dashboarding: Console chart with per-model pad_saved and alert if pad_saved drops >50% relative to canary baseline (indicates regression).
